payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Add a helmet to the woman.
node.criteria: Apply the original rubric to the requested change only. Return yes when the evidence establishes that the woman has a helmet on her head and that adding it is a requested edit. Return no only when the evidence establishes that no requested change has progressed. Return partial when evidence establishes some progress toward adding the helmet but does not establish complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits do not count as progress. If the evidence does not establish which rubric outcome applies, return unknown. The endpoint inspection can establish completion on its own when it clearly shows the requested result; the comparison check is supporting evidence, not an additional completion requirement. If that check is skipped, do not treat it as not applicable or as a failure: use the endpoint evidence to decide whether completion is established, and otherwise return unknown unless other evidence establishes progress or no progress. Supporting observations do not earn completion credit independently.
node.binding: Target: The woman is wearing or otherwise visibly has a helmet on her head.. Reference: The woman in the input image..

node_traces.evidence: The endpoint evidence establishes that the woman is wearing a helmet, completing the requested edit.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image clearly shows the woman wearing a helmet on her head.
Comparing the images, the edited image shows a helmet on the woman's head that is absent in the source image.

response.content: {"text":"The node is already performing well: the edited image visibly shows a helmet on the woman’s head, and the source comparison supports that it was added; the trace is complete with high confidence and the aggregate matches the reference. No semantic change is indicated. For robustness, preserve the distinction between endpoint evidence establishing completion and comparison evidence serving only as support; do not make both checks mandatory or infer failure from a skipped check. The abbreviated binding should remain unambiguous about the woman as the target, but there is no observed binding error here."}
